paper.title: Gender and socioeconomic dimensions of relative age effects on ADHD prescriptions: Evidence from Denmark
paper.code_data_availability: Data availability (p. 3): 'The authors do not have permission to share data.' No replication code, DST project number or register application reference is given.

registers.role: sample frame; treatment (date of birth); controls (household type, geographical region, ancestry); linkage (identifies the children's parents)
controls and subgroup split: the parents' yearly taxable / personal annual income
outcome: whether an individual was prescribed any ADHD medicine
variables_mentioned: ATC codes C02AC02, N06BA02, N06BA04, N06BA09, N06BA12 (Statistics Denmark's definition of ADHD medicine)

linkages: Children linked to their parents via the Danish National Population Registry ('it is used to identify the children's parents'), which allows parental income from the Income Statistic to be attached to each child
Children linked to their ADHD prescriptions via the Danish National Prescription Registry at the individual level

sample.universe: All Danish children aged 6-16 from 2010 to 2019 (the paper notes this includes some individuals not in school and excludes some still in school)
selection_rules: Regression sample restricted to children born within 100 days of January 1 (days_i in [-100, 100])
Estimated separately for boys and girls
Heterogeneity: the girls' sample split by whether the mother's or the father's personal annual income is below or above the sample median
Robustness: the girls' sample split into the subperiods 2010-2014 and 2015-2019
Fig. 2 (school starting age) uses the years 2010-2013; Fig. 3 (ADHD rate by age) uses children in school 2010-2019
sample.n_observations: 1 579 596 boy-years and 1 504 509 girl-years within 100 days of the cutoff (Table 1); 752 250 / 752 259 girl-years below / above the mother's median income and 749 880 / 754 629 below / above the father's median income (Table 2); 754 451 girl-years in 2010-2014 and 750 058 in 2015-2019 (Table 3)

construction_notes: ADHD_it is 1 if individual i has a prescription for ADHD medicine at time t; the definition follows a recent analysis by Statistics Denmark (2023) and is based on five ATC codes: C02AC02, N06BA02, N06BA04, N06BA09 and N06BA12
The definition does not take into consideration how many prescriptions a given individual has used or how much of the active drug is prescribed
days_i is the difference in days between birth date and the cutoff: days_i = -1, 0, 1 means born December 31, January 1, January 2
Only children born within 100 days of January 1 are used (|days_i| <= 100)

f(days_i) is a polynomial fit of second degree, fitted separately on either side of the cutoff: f(days_i) = phi0 + phi1 days_i + phi2 days_i^2 + phi3[days_i * I(days_i >= 0)] + phi4[days_i^2 * I(days_i >= 0)]
X_it is a vector of observable characteristics: the parents' personal income, the child's home region, type of household, and ancestry

In Fig. 1 one observation is a five-day average of ADHD prescription rates, plotted by five-day intervals of days_i; alpha_1 corresponds exactly to the vertical distance between the two polynomial fits at the cutoff

School starting age (Fig. 2) is an approximation based on when a person graduated 6th grade, and is biased upward for children who retook a grade before 6th grade (around 2.5% were retakers in 0th grade in 2019)
Standard errors are clustered at the days level in all reported regressions

claims.statement: Among Danish boys, being born on or after January 1 (and therefore being the oldest rather than the youngest in the class) does not significantly change the probability of having an ADHD prescription.

treatment.label: I(days_i >= 0): born on or after January 1, i.e. one day later than December 31, and therefore the oldest rather than the youngest in the class

register_source.value: The Danish National Population Registry (date of birth); no register code or variable name given in the paper

definition.value: Indicator equal to 1 if the child is born on or after January 1. days_i is the difference in days between the birth date and the cutoff, so days_i = -1, 0, 1 means born December 31, January 1, January 2; only children born within 100 days of January 1 are used. Because Danish children should start school in the calendar year they turn six, children born December 31 start school a full year earlier than children born January 1 and are the youngest in their class, while the latter are the oldest.

timing.value: Fixed at birth; school entry is determined by the calendar year the child turns six, and the outcome is observed while the child is aged 6-16 in 2010-2019

outcome.label: ADHD_it: indicator equal to 1 if individual i has a prescription for ADHD medicine at time t

register_source.value: The Danish National Prescription Registry (used to determine whether an individual was prescribed any ADHD medicine); no register code or variable name given in the paper

definition.value: Binary child-year indicator for having a prescription for ADHD medicine. ADHD medicine follows the Statistics Denmark (2023) definition, based on five ATC codes: C02AC02, N06BA02, N06BA04, N06BA09 and N06BA12. The definition does not take into consideration how many prescriptions a given individual has used or how much of the active drug is prescribed.

timing.value: Measured contemporaneously in each child-year, children aged 6-16, 2010-2019

units.value: probability of having an ADHD prescription in a given child-year (binary dependent variable ADHD_it); -0.0015 corresponds to -0.15 percentage points

magnitude.interpretation: The paper reports 'a drop in ADHD prescription rates at the cutoff for both genders' but states that 'Our estimates are only significant for girls.'

The paper estimates the reduced form of a fuzzy RD design at this January 1 birth-date cutoff.
